articles.title: Stranger Than Heaven Features Optional “Cheats” to Make its Combat Easier
articles.summary: Stranger Than Heaven, the upcoming street-brawler from the makers of Yakuza and Like a Dragon, will feature optional in-game assists to make its challenging new combat system more approachable, developer RGG Studio has confirmed to IGN in an interview conducted at Gamescom Asia x Thailand Game Show…
body: In IGN’s most recent hands-on with the game, my colleague Michael Higham described Stranger Than Heaven’s parry-based combat system as “demanding”, adding that “you really have to pay attention to attack animations not just for timing, but to make the correct call on the direction it's coming from.” This initially seemed like it could prove to be divisive among fans of the comparatively carefree button-mashing combo systems found in RRG Studios’ previous adventures like Like a Dragon: Pirate Yakuza in Hawaii and Lost Judgment, but it turns out that Stranger Than Heaven’s more complex combat system will only be as difficult as players want it to be.

articles.title: Monster Hunter Outlanders Review So Far
articles.summary: This mobile spin-off maintains the gameplay loop and visuals of its console counterparts, with the caveat of how progress gates push microtransactions.
body: Like most Monster Hunter games, Outlanders begins with a big cinematic opening where a group of adventurers from the Adventurer's Guild are striking out to an uncharted part of the world – in this case, an island called Aesoland. This island is filled with Radiant species of monsters, beasts whose abilities have been enhanced by a mineral called Radiantite. This is, ostensibly, also the game's reasoning for creating new designs of classic series monsters and tweaking their abilities to match this game specifically, like the Pukei-Pukei focusing more on head or tail attacks, which are easier to target with Outlander's more streamlined lock-on system.

articles.title: 15 Classic Games That Prove Gameplay Is More Important Than Graphics
articles.summary: There’s no getting around it: graphics matter a great deal for video games. For many years, visual fidelity alone was one of the best reasons to invest in new consoles and better gaming PCs. There have always been games that didn’t compete for a position at the head of the pack, though.
body: As we look forward to the visual powerhouse that is Grand Theft Auto 6, here are 15 classic games that prove great graphics aren’t everything — and in many ways make the case that good gameplay is a more important factor for timelessness.

N+ is the console version of N, a game originally developed as an Adobe Flash game, but Metanet Software partnered with other developers to produce a version for Xbox Live Arcade. The game features extremely simple controls that allow players to run and leap around hundreds of stages in treacherous, mostly barren environments. It’s not a visual stunner, but the gameplay loop kept players coming back for dozens of hours.

Final Fantasy games have tended to push visual boundaries, one after another. Following on the heels of Final Fantasy 8, which featured realistic models for its memorable cast of characters, Final Fantasy 9 went in a different direction. Its chibi characters were expressive and the world beautiful, but in some respects it felt like a visual regression that Final Fantasy 10 rectified one year later. Even in a world with gorgeous stunners like Final Fantasy 16, this much older title remains a delight to play.

articles.title: Chronicles: Medieval Developer 'At Real Risk of Closing' Before Release as Funding 'No Longer in Place'
articles.summary: Chronicles: Medieval developer Raw Power Games posted a chilling warning on its social media pages, warning that the studio might close before it can launch the Early Access version of its medieval open-world action/strategy sandbox because funding for the team is "no longer in place." In a message…
body: In a message on X (with a hat tip to Insider Gaming ), Raw Power laid out its unfortunate predicament: "Due to circumstances outside our control, the necessary funding behind Raw Power Games is no longer in place. Without it we can't keep building Chronicles: Medieval, and right now the studio is at real risk of closing. We're not going to sugarcoat. You deserve to hear it plainly, and directly from us.

"What makes it hurt is how close we are," the message continued. "Early Access is within reach. The world we've been building for years is finally starting to feel alive, and we have so much we've been thrilled to show you. Every day in the studio – in Copenhagen and remote – we've seen people put everything they have into this game, often far beyond what anyone asked of them. They are the ones carrying the heaviest weight right now, and we couldn't be prouder of them. We don't know yet how this ends. But in the spirit of our game we're not going down without a fight!"

articles.title: Xbox's Doom, Wolfenstein Developers Working 'More Closely Than Ever' Following Xbox 'Reset' Layoffs
articles.summary: Bethesda and Xbox development studio id Software, maker of the Doom franchise, has deepened its partnership with fellow Bethesda and Xbox studio MachineGames, makers of the most recent Wolfenstein games as well as 2024's Indiana Jones and the Great Circle.
body: At a press event earlier this week for id Software's Doom: The Dark Ages - Revelations DLC, which was released this summer, studio co-director Marty Stratton was asked how the studio is doing in the wake of the layoffs that affected id as part of Xbox CEO Asha Sharma's ongoing Xbox " reset." He answered, "We're doing great. Not to handwave the [layoffs] away...everybody knows we had about half of our studio exit as part of that. But there was a very deliberate effort to make sure that we were incredibly viable coming out of that across everything we do, across game development and technology department.

"We're working more closely with MachineGames than ever. We've always had a very close partnership with them, but I think we're at a point with technology development that both teams are incredibly talented and have incredibly talented engineers and we're really on an amazing path that had started pre-[layoffs]. We'd kicked this off earlier this year. We're really excited about that. We're both really really bullish on what we have ahead."

articles.title: Top 10 Pokémon Cards Most Likely to Be Fake
articles.summary: The more Pokémon trading cards pop off, the more potential players and collectors have to worry about one thing: counterfeit cards. Sometimes, a fake card will be obvious. As more money pours into the hobby, however, there's more incentive than ever to pull a fast one on people.
body: Grading service PSA recently published a fraud report that goes over trends in forged and altered collectibles, including Pokémon cards. As PSA is in the business of assessing card conditions and determining their value, the service needs to be good at spotting counterfeits. According to the report, 2025 saw an incredible 407% increase in altered Pokémon cards attempting to be graded.

The specific characters that swindlers target likely won't be a surprise, but it's still worth knowing which cards should warrant a second look IRL. It's easy to assume only the most expensive and elusive cards on the market would be in contention, but that's not the case. The top card can be purchased for $150 or under. It makes sense, though: It's harder to pass off an ultra-rare card as legitimate. It's also difficult to sell a card that's the equivalent to a down payment on a house.
points: The more Pokémon trading cards pop off, the more potential players and collectors have to worry about one thing: counterfeit cards.
As more money pours into the hobby, however, there's more incentive than ever to pull a fast one on people.

articles.title: Every Mike Flanagan TV Series, Ranked
articles.summary: Mike Flanagan is certainly having a moment this year. After the success of Prime Video's Carrie — and its season two renewal — more eyes are on him and his works than ever before. Luckily, he has a fairly solid backlog of TV shows and films for viewers to peruse.
body: One of the strongest traits of his work is how much it speaks to the human condition, and how well he is able to weave the horror elements into those stories. It's also just a fact that Flanagan hasn't worked on a "bad" show. Each new one has brought a different flavor of grief, connection, and just straight-up horror. From haunted houses and familial trauma to existential supernatural drama, Flanagan has made a name for himself within the genre.

Based on Christopher Pike's YA novel, The Midnight Club follows a group of terminally ill teenagers in a hospice manor who meet after dark to share spooky tales, much like a modern Are You Afraid of the Dark? Co-created with Leah Fong, The Midnight Club is a deviation from Flanagan's normal form. Originally designed to be a continuing series, Netflix unfortunately canceled it after one season, denying any hopes of a natural conclusion for the story.

articles.title: EA Just Shelved A Mysterious Sims Project—That Could Be Good News For Players
articles.summary: It's been another rough year for video games, with countless studio closures, staff layoffs, and projects that barely managed to even get off the ground before they were unceremoniously cut short.
body: This was especially painful for Mass Effect players, who were looking forward to the upcoming Mass Effect 5, which we now know was tentatively titled Mass Effect: Universe. But it's not just BioWare fans who are upset at the moment. Fans of EA's other properties are growing increasingly concerned about the future of those franchises, if any future is planned for them at all. My colleague Levi Winslow recently wrote about their concerns for the Skate franchise in the wake of layoffs at its development studio. Meanwhile, I'm quite worried about the fate of The Sims.

In the same breath it announced the end of BioWare, EA also reaffirmed its commitment to Apex Legends, Skate, and The Sims franchises. But everyone knows that when it comes to profits, EA's sports titles outrun its other IPs by a country mile. If EA is willing to pull the plug on legacy franchises like Mass Effect and Dragon Age, where does that leave its other franchises, like The Sims 4?
points: It's been another rough year for video games, with countless studio closures, staff layoffs, and projects that barely managed to even get off the ground before they were unceremoniously cut short.

articles.summary: If you do your research, though, you’ll find a treasure trove of easily-accessible gems — like a solo dev’s reworked Diablo village where you watch your party auto-battle its way through catacombs, or an idle game where managing catnip supply chains spirals into deep-space civilization management.
body: All of these games cost the exact same amount: Nothing. Pull one up in your browser right now — no sunk cost, no download, no account to make. Bookmark whichever ones pull you in. You won’t pay anything, but you might lose countless hours to catnip management or paperclip production on these free browser games. Don’t say we didn’t warn you.
Play this if: You like Slay the Spire, but wish the cards were dice instead.

Die in the Dungeon Classic swaps your familiar rogue deckbuilder game’s cards for dice. In this game, you play a frog warrior descending through a dungeon, placing attack (red), defense (blue), heal (green), and boost (purple) dice onto a diamond-shaped grid each turn. Some dice stick around for multiple turns. Others shatter after a single use. Will you think ahead or go with a flashier instant-gratification strategy? What’s not a roll of the dice is this game’s impression — it’s currently sitting at a 4.7-star rating across nearly 3,000 ratings on itch.io.
Play this if: You like Diablo -style dungeon crawls, but want to watch your party handle it instead of doing it yourself.

articles.title: CoD: Modern Warfare To Cut Real-Life Korean Tragedy Segment After Backlash
articles.summary: Publisher Activision has responded to criticism over using a devastating tragedy in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, saying that the incident will be removed from the military shooter in a November 12 update. The Seoul Halloween crowd crush occurred in October 2022 in Itaewon.
body: "Using such an incident as material for a game intended for entertainment purposes is itself highly inappropriate and a senseless act," the groups said, according to the BBC. "The Itaewon tragedy was a tragic disaster that produced hundreds of casualties, and citizens who participated in the rescue efforts or witnessed the event at the time continue to suffer from trauma. If the game developer has even a minimum level of courtesy and empathy toward the victims, they should promptly take corrective measures."

Activision has heard the call and plans to remove the depiction from Modern Warfare 4 when an update arrives on November 12. In responding to the criticism, Activision said it never intended to trivialize the disaster or make light of human suffering.

"In developing Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4, we approached the subject matter with care and respect. The game’s opening cinematic utilises some real-world news coverage to establish the game’s fictional narrative," Activision said. "It is not intended to reference or trivialise the Itaewon disaster or any other real-world tragedy in any way, shape or form."

articles.title: GOTY hopeful Mina the Hollower bought the studio financial stability "for now," while the Shovel Knight devs work on a new 3D game
articles.summary: Yacht Club Games has confirmed that most of its developers are now working on a brand new 3D game (potentially Shovel Knight 3D), after the critically-acclaimed Mina the Hollower did well enough for the team to continue.
body: Before launching its old-school adventure game earlier this year, Yacht Club described Mina the Hollower as a "make-or-break" moment for the beloved indie studio. A global pandemic and a failed experiment to turn Yacht Club into a multi-project studio had left the developer on thin ice, it seems.

But Mina the Hollower sold well enough to buy the studio more time, according to a new Reddit AMA full of interesting tidbits. Asked if Mina was able to secure financial stability for the company, Sean Velasco simply said "yes… for now!" Mina managed to sell over 500,000 copies in its first two weeks, so it's well on its way to the one million copies the devs were once hoping for.

For the foreseeable future, the devs aren't ready to talk about the kinds of DLC and spin-offs and follow-ups that dear old Shovel Knight enjoyed for many years, but they're not abandoning their newest baby either. "We're working on more post-release features," the devs wrote, which includes "expanded randomizer options, enemy and boss randomization, more modifiers, speedrunner features" and more ways "to do even more in Mina."

articles.title: New Assassin’s Creed Game Is Out Now, If You Don’t Mind Being Board
articles.summary: If you thought there wasn't going to be a new Assassin's Creed game this year, think again. It's not a video game, but Assassin's Creed: Animus is out today, turning the series into an adventure-style board game for 1-4 players.
body: A competitive game that pits players against each other as they explore distinct eras from the video games, Assassin's Creed: Animus features four protagonists to choose from in its standard edition: Eivor, Ezio, Altair, and Connor. The Collector's Edition, meanwhile, expands to 10 eras and features 16 protagonists, adding game characters like Edward Kenway, Jacob and Evie Frye, and Kassandra.

You and up to three of your friends (or you alone) work to complete objectives across these eras, taking down assassination targets in the way you see fit via "memory blocks." Whether you go in with your sword drawn or engage in a sneakier approach is up to you.

The standard version of Assassin's Creed: Animus is available to order now for $65, while the limited Collector's Edition costs $229. Alongside the extra characters and eras, this version comes with a storage box, acrylic tokens, a metal Piece of Eden, a cloth token bag, "special event cards," and an Animus Card Holder.

articles.title: Blizzard hints at console ports for World of Warcraft: Forever - "Play it wherever you want and, at some point, on whatever you want"
articles.summary: After more than two decades dominating the PC MMO battlefield, it sounds like Blizzard Entertainment 's taking the idea of a World of Warcraft console port more seriously than ever.
body: World of Warcraft: Forever's beta seems to have been immensely popular with fans of the series. It's a brand new third version of the iconic multiplayer game that sits alongside WoW's Classic and Retail portions, and it's recaptured many a lapsed Warcraft sicko with tons of good changes, big and small - one of which is controller support for the first time ever.

Speaking to GamesRadar about the decision to keep World of Warcraft: Forever exclusive to PC players, despite now supporting gamepads, vice president and executive producer Holly Longdale hinted that the fantasy game might just make its way to even more devices and players over time.

"What you just described is really what we're after," she told the outlet. "Play it wherever you want and, at some point, on whatever you want. But the first leg of that journey is getting gamepads working really well with World of Warcraft, and we thought Forever was the perfect place to start."

articles.title: Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3's online servers are temporarily going dark, FromSoftware announces
articles.summary: Things might get even darker over in the world of Lordran without those silly, only sometimes helpful notes left by other players. Developer FromSoftware has announced that it's temporarily closing Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3 servers because of an unspecified issue.
body: "Due to a server issue, the game servers for the following titles will be temporarily unavailable on all platforms," the RPG studio tweeted earlier today, before naming Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3.

While the server shutdown won't last forever, FromSoftware hasn't told series fans when exactly they can expect online play to be restored. That presumably means PvP invasions, summon signs and in-game messages that try to troll you off a cliff are unavailable for the time being.
"We will provide updates once we have information regarding the server restoration time. We apologize for the inconvenience," the studio added. I hope you've stocked up on Estus Flasks, at least.

Of course, this isn't the first time the Dark Souls trilogy has had to contend with server problems. In 2022, Bandai Namco took servers for all three Dark Souls games offline due to a security vulnerability affecting Dark Souls 3. The threequel went dark once again a few months later.
points: Developer FromSoftware has announced that it's temporarily closing Dark Souls 2 and Dark Souls 3 servers because of an unspecified issue.

videos.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 DMZ Review
videos.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4's DMZ mode reviewed by Jarrett Green on PlayStation 5, also available on Xbox Series X|S, Nintendo Switch 2, and PC.
body: "Modern Warfare 4’s DMZ mode finally puts the fun and frantic gunplay signature to Call of Duty into a genre I fancy more than its typical PvP multiplayer. While executing missions, the semi-arcadey running and gunning mixes nicely with the vibrant exploration elements in Hajin and the rapid fire Dynamic Objectives and side ops, creating a delightfully high-tension experience that also doesn’t get too sweaty. All of the other things around it – crafting, gunsmithing, and to a larger extent the almost RPG-like skill trees for individual operators – provide little incentive to engage with them all that rigorously. This may not bode well for DMZ’s staying power as a “service” across the coming year, but in the present, it’s a strong addition to the growing list of worthwhile extraction shooters."

videos.summary: Watch the final 'From the Ward' episode for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for a behind-the-scenes look at the making of the first-person shooter game and the process of creating live seasons.
body: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is available now on PlayStation 5 (PS5), Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC (Steam).
points: Watch the final 'From the Ward' episode for Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 for a behind-the-scenes look at the making of the first-person shooter game and the process of creating live seasons.
Join the development team at Infinity Ward as they discuss what's ahead with live seasons, and how stories, characters, Multiplayer, DMZ, and Call of Duty: Warzone come together in the journey ahead.
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is available now on PlayStation 5 (PS5), Nintendo Switch 2, Xbox Series X|S, and PC (Steam).
